sections.h2: Where is Newtown, Connecticut, and how big is it?
sections.html:
Newtown is a town in northern Fairfield County, about 45 miles southwest of Hartford and 42 miles northeast of New York City. It is part of the Greater Danbury area and the Western Connecticut Planning Region, and the Census Bureau counted 27,173 residents in 2020.

The town covers roughly 58 square miles of land, which makes it the fifth largest town in the state by area. The Housatonic River forms its northeastern border, and Newtown touches Bethel, Bridgewater, Brookfield, Easton, Monroe, Oxford, Redding and Southbury.

Local zoning outside the central borough uses a minimum lot of one acre, so houses in most of town sit on larger parcels than in a coastal city.

sections.h2: How did Newtown grow, and what does that history mean for its houses?
sections.html:
English colonists bought the townsite in 1705 from the Pohtatuck people, and Newtown was incorporated in 1711. The population passed 4,000 around 1881, dropped to a low of 2,635 in 1930, and then rose steadily after World War II as the town became a suburb of Danbury, with commuters also traveling to Norwalk, Stamford and Bridgeport.

The census counts show how quickly it grew: the population went from 7,448 in 1950 to 16,942 in 1970 and 25,031 in 2000.

Houses built during that post-war growth are now decades old, and an owner who does not want to replace a septic system, furnace or roof before listing has the option of a buyer who takes the house as it is.

sections.h2: What are the villages and areas inside Newtown?
sections.html:
Newtown is organized around several named villages rather than one downtown. The main communities are Botsford, Dodgingtown, Hattertown, Hawleyville, Sandy Hook and the Newtown Borough, with smaller areas such as Taunton, Head of Meadow, Huntingtown and Middle Gate.

  • Newtown Borough and Hawleyville share ZIP code 06470 along with Botsford.
  • Sandy Hook, including Berkshire, Riverside, Walnut Tree Hill and Zoar, uses ZIP code 06482.
  • Hawleyville was an important railroad crossroads for a time in the town's history.

Telling a buyer which village your house is in helps them understand the commute, the school zone and the lot size to expect.

sections.h2: What is the Newtown Borough, and why does it matter for sellers?
sections.html:
The Borough of Newtown is a small separate municipality inside the town, covering about 1,252 acres in the center, and it is one of only nine boroughs in Connecticut. It was incorporated in 1824 by the General Assembly.

Services inside the borough are different from the rest of town. The borough has public water from the Water and Sewer Authority and much of it is sewered, while most of the rest of Newtown relies on private wells and septic systems. Borough zoning also allows lot sizes smaller than the one-acre minimum used across the rest of the community.

If your house is outside the borough, expect a buyer to ask about the well and septic system, including the age and condition of each. Those two items often drive repair negotiations on rural Connecticut sales.

The Newtown Economic Development Commission lists the Board of Education, the town government and a mix of private and state employers as the largest in the area. Named employers include Masonicare at Newtown, now the Newtown Rehabilitation and Healthcare Center, the state Department of Correction at Garner, Taunton Press, Charter Communications, Big Y, Tier One Manufacturing, Newtown Savings Bank, Curtis Packaging, Vodafone, Caraluzzi's Newtown Market, Stop and Shop, Sonics and Materials, Rand-Whitney and Mediassociates.

Many residents also work outside town, in Danbury and in the Fairfield County coastal cities. For a seller, that means buyers may be weighing a commute to those places.

Newtown Public Schools runs four elementary schools for kindergarten through grade 4, one intermediate school, one middle school and one high school. The elementary schools are Hawley, Head O'Meadow, Middle Gate and Sandy Hook.

  • Reed Intermediate School serves grades 5 and 6.
  • Newtown Middle School serves grades 7 and 8.
  • Newtown High School serves grades 9 through 12.

Private and parochial options include St. Rose of Lima, the Fraser-Woods Montessori School and the Housatonic Valley Waldorf School. Sellers often mention the school zone in the listing, so know which elementary school your street feeds.

sections.h2: How are Newtown's property taxes billed?
sections.html:
Newtown bills real estate tax in two installments, July and January, and the current mill rate on the 2025 Grand List is 29.26. A bill under $50 is due in one installment in July.

ItemWhat the Newtown Tax Collector says
First installmentDue in July, last day without penalty is August 1 unless it falls on a weekend
Second installmentDue in January, last day without penalty is February 1 unless it falls on a weekend
Mill rate, 2025 Grand List29.26
Delinquent interest18% per year, 1.5% per month, $2 minimum per installment
Mailed paymentsOn time if postmarked by the last day to pay

The Tax Collector also bills sewer and water use charges and benefit assessments, so a final balance check before closing should cover those. The office phone is 203-270-4320.

sections.h2: What does a Newtown seller owe at closing to the state?
sections.html:
Connecticut charges a conveyance tax on the deed. For a residential sale the state portion is three-quarters of one percent and the municipal portion is one-quarter of one percent, so a $450,000 house would produce $4,500 in tax at those base rates.

  • A higher state rate applies to the part of a residential price over $800,000.
  • The grantor, the grantor's attorney or the grantor's agent files Form OP-236 when the deed is recorded.
  • Exemptions exist, such as a transfer between spouses or a deed in lieu of foreclosure on a principal residence.

An added municipal rate of up to one-quarter of one percent is allowed for targeted investment communities, so confirm with the Newtown Town Clerk whether anything beyond the base rate applies.

sections.h2: What is the town government structure for permits and approvals?
sections.html:
Newtown is led by a First Selectman and a Board of Selectmen, and a 12-member Legislative Council passes ordinances and approves budgets. The final budget goes to a town-wide referendum.

This matters to sellers only when a project is pending, such as an open permit, a zoning question or an unfinished addition. Ask the town offices about any open permits before you sign a contract, because an unresolved one can hold up a conventional closing.

sections.h2: Which ways of selling fit Newtown houses?
sections.html:
Most Newtown owners choose between listing with an agent and selling to a cash buyer, depending on how much preparation they can do.

  • A listing suits a house in good shape where you can wait for the right buyer.
  • A cash sale suits an estate, a tenant-occupied house, or a property with a failing septic system or other deferred work.
  • Cash Home Buyers purchases Newtown houses as they stand, so there is nothing to repair first.

Request a no-obligation cash offer and compare it with what an agent estimates for your address.

faqs.q: How much is the Newtown mill rate?
faqs.a: The Newtown Tax Collector lists the current mill rate on the 2025 Grand List as 29.26. Multiply your assessed value by the mill rate and divide by 1,000 to estimate the annual bill.

faqs.q: When are Newtown property taxes due?
faqs.a: Real estate tax can be paid in two installments, July and January. The last day to pay without penalty is usually August 1 and February 1, moved if the date falls on a weekend.

faqs.q: Does Newtown use septic systems and wells?
faqs.a: Many properties do. The central Borough of Newtown has public water and much of it is sewered, but most of the rest of town relies on wells and septic systems.

faqs.q: What conveyance tax will I pay selling in Newtown?
faqs.a: At the base rates, residential conveyance tax is three-quarters of one percent state plus one-quarter of one percent municipal. The grantor files Form OP-236 at recording. Ask the Town Clerk about any additional municipal rate.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Newtown house with a failing septic system?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer can purchase as-is, so you do not need to replace the system before selling. The price will reflect the repair.
Newtown Public Schools serves the town, with four elementary schools, Reed Intermediate, Newtown Middle School and Newtown High School.
